summary: Execute and Undo. Wrap a reversible action and let the history walk it back and forth.
purpose: The standard Command pattern. Not UI-specific despite living beside the UI tools — it works for a level editor's placement tool or a form's revert button equally.
whenToImplement: When an action needs to be reversible. If it cannot be undone cleanly, it does not belong in the history at all.

Execute().contract: Do the action. Called once when first executed, and again on every redo, so it must produce the same result each time.
Execute().mustNot: Do not capture the state you need to undo INSIDE Execute. Capture it at construction — by redo time the world has already changed.

Undo().contract: Put things back exactly as they were. Called with the world in the state Execute left it.
Undo().mustNot: Do not assume Execute ran immediately before. Several commands may have been undone in between, so undo must depend only on state captured at construction.

calledBy: CommandHistory: Execute when first run and on every redo, Undo when walking back. Nothing else should call either — calling Execute directly bypasses the history and makes undo inconsistent.
useCases: Placing and removing objects in an editor.
A property change that should be revertible.
Batched operations undone as one step.

gotchas.title: Redo re-runs Execute, it does not replay a recording
gotchas.body: So Execute must be repeatable and must not depend on the state it happens to find.
